findings.finding: The plan gives no fallback if pangolin's `tests/_exe_stub.py` is not on main when the other 10 fixes are ready, or if a fixed test still fails in the Windows validation run. The executor cannot tell whether to block the whole ticket or ship 10 fixes and leave the reclaim line. AC2's only escape hatch, 'intentionally unsupported on Windows', mislabels a test that is merely blocked or whose fix did not work.
findings.location: Approach step 6 ('This waits for pangolin's change on main') / Acceptance Criteria AC2
scenarios: Pangolin slips by a week. The executor either idles or ships 10 fixes, then cannot satisfy AC2 for the reclaim test because it is not 'intentionally unsupported'.
A fix (e.g. the git archive one) still fails on the Windows runner. AC2 forces a false 'unsupported' label instead of re-iteration.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a note (PR description or contributor doc) telling existing Windows clones to re-checkout the two pinned files after pulling (e.g. `git rm --cached <files> && git checkout -- <files>`), or acknowledge that the fix applies only to fresh checkouts.
evidence: "mark the 2 vendored pinned files `-text` so no checkout converts them. Their blobs are LF today (`ls-files --eol` shows `i/lf`), so the bytes are unchanged."
Git fact: changing .gitattributes does not re-smudge working-tree files whose blobs did not change; a re-checkout or `git add --renormalize` is needed.
findings.finding: Marking the two pinned vendored files `-text` in .gitattributes only changes newly checked-out files. Existing Windows clones under core.autocrlf=true keep their CRLF working-tree copies after pulling the fix, because the blobs are unchanged ('so the bytes are unchanged'), so git does not rewrite them. Their SHA-256 pins keep failing locally.
scenarios: Windows developer workstation with an existing clone: after `git pull`, test_jira_dc_harness_shape, test_bridge_provider_wrappers and test_reconcile_workflow_lint still fail with SHA-256 mismatches, although CI (fresh checkout) is green.
findings.suggested_fix: In the PR/merge notes, tell existing Windows clones to run: `git rm --cached tests/external/live_jira_dc/pycontribs-jira-LICENSE.txt .github/schemas/gitlab-ci.schema.json && git checkout -- tests/external/live_jira_dc/pycontribs-jira-LICENSE.txt .github/schemas/gitlab-ci.schema.json`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In gitutil.py, leave TimeoutExpired.output/.stderr as the bytes the stdlib already provides (re-raise unchanged after reaping) instead of decoding them only on the str-input path.
evidence: Plan: 'Only then apply check, raising CalledProcessError with the decoded str. A TimeoutExpired gets its output/stderr decoded the same way.'
gitutil.py:250-254 _run_in_group reaps the process group and re-raises communicate's TimeoutExpired unchanged, so its payload is whatever the stdlib attaches (bytes on POSIX).

Callers that catch TimeoutExpired from run_git (delta_tree.py:207, _ref_lock.py:216, run_git_bounded:309) do not read .output, so decoding has no consumer but still changes the exception contract for one input type.
findings.finding: The plan decodes TimeoutExpired.output/.stderr to str only on the new str-input path. The stdlib documents these attributes as always bytes, even with text=True. run_git(timeout=...) calls without input_data, or with bytes input_data, will keep raising bytes payloads. The exception's payload type would then depend on the input_data type, and on POSIX the change differs from today's behavior even though the plan says returned text will be 'identical on POSIX'.
findings.location: Approach §1 (src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py), bullet 'A TimeoutExpired gets its output/stderr decoded the same way'
scenarios: Code that formats exc.output from a run_git timeout gets bytes when no stdin was given and str when str stdin was given, so code written for one type breaks on the other.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the TimeoutExpired-decoding bullet: on the str-input binary path, let TimeoutExpired propagate unchanged (after the existing reap), so its payload matches the stdlib's always-bytes contract and every other run_git path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In Approach §1, state why the product rewrite beats the cheaper option (document that str stdin is translated on Windows and point newline-sensitive callers to text=False). Or narrow the change to the str-stdin path and keep it as small as possible.
evidence: Plan: "No shipped caller is affected today: `reconciler/_ref_lock.py` already hashes bytes with `text=False`, and `_snapshot/delta_tree.py`'s checkout-index payload is NUL-separated."

grep `input_data=` in src/rebar finds only delta_tree.py:204 (NUL-joined str payload), reclaim_collapse.py:267 (its `_git` wrapper types input_data as `bytes | None`, line 259) and reconciler/_ref_lock.py:211 (bytes).

gitutil.py:185-189 already documents the text/bytes stdin contract; the alternative is to say in that docstring that str stdin is newline-translated on Windows and steer newline-sensitive callers to text=False, as _ref_lock.py already does.
findings.finding: The run_git/_run_in_group rewrite (binary mode, hand-written universal-newline decode, manual check, TimeoutExpired decode) is justified only by the documented str-stdin contract and one unit test. The plan itself says no shipped caller is affected, so this is complexity for a hypothetical caller (YAGNI) unless the plan explicitly gives the contract as the reason.
scenarios: A reviewer or maintainer later sees a hand-written decode/check path in the store's central git seam with no product caller that needs it and cannot tell why it exists.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In Approach §1, say that both paths build a CompletedProcess with the decoded stdout/stderr and call `result.check_returncode()`, as gitutil.py:255-257 already does, instead of raising CalledProcessError by hand.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:255-257: `result = subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, proc.returncode, stdout, stderr)` / `if check: result.check_returncode()`
Plan: "Only then apply `check`, raising `CalledProcessError` with the decoded str."
findings.finding: The plan says to apply `check` by hand after decoding, "raising `CalledProcessError` with the decoded str". gitutil already has this mechanism: `_run_in_group` builds a `subprocess.CompletedProcess` and calls `result.check_returncode()`, which raises CalledProcessError carrying the result's stdout/stderr. The plan should reuse that step instead of writing new raise logic.
findings.location: Approach §1, bullet "Only then apply `check`, raising `CalledProcessError` with the decoded str"
scenarios: A hand-written `raise CalledProcessError(...)` leaves out `output`/`stderr`, or sets them differently from the stdlib, so the run_git path and the _run_in_group path raise errors with different fields.
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach §1, replace the bullet with: "Decode stdout/stderr into a `subprocess.CompletedProcess`, then `if check: result.check_returncode()` — the same step `_run_in_group` already uses (gitutil.py:255-257) — so both paths raise an identical stdlib CalledProcessError carrying str."

tests/unit/test_run_git_wrapper.py:95 and :106 already test str and bytes stdin.

findings.suggested_fix: In Approach, change "`tests/unit/test_run_git_stdin_bytes.py`" to "new cases in `tests/unit/test_run_git_wrapper.py`" and remove `tests/unit/test_run_git_stdin_bytes.py` from Scope.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Dispatch the Windows validation by workflow filename (`gh workflow run test.yml --ref tmp/b4-neglectful-acceptable-gerbil`), or confirm 294845723 is test.yml's ID, and confirm the recorded run contains a `sweep (windows)` job.
evidence: Plan: "dispatch `gh workflow run 294845723 --ref tmp/b4-neglectful-acceptable-gerbil`"
search_files for '294845723' finds it only in a plan-review cache file, never in .github/ or the docs. Evidence class: Unverified.
Elsewhere the repo dispatches by filename: release.yml:382 `gh workflow run autobump.yml`, reconcile-bridge.yml:309 `gh workflow run reconcile-bridge.yml --ref ...`.
test.yml has `workflow_dispatch:` (line 18) and runs the Windows sweep jobs on workflow_dispatch (lines 262, 296). Dispatching by filename works and is unambiguous.
findings.finding: The validation step dispatches by a numeric workflow ID (`gh workflow run 294845723`) that nothing in the repo confirms is `.github/workflows/test.yml`. If the ID is stale or points to another workflow, the dispatched run would not be the `sweep (windows)` run the Testing section and AC1 depend on, and its run id could still be recorded as evidence.
scenarios: The ID belongs to a renamed or different workflow, so the dispatched run has no `sweep (windows)` job, or validates a different job, and its id is recorded as Windows validation.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `gh workflow run 294845723 --ref tmp/b4-neglectful-acceptable-gerbil` with `gh workflow run test.yml --ref tmp/b4-neglectful-acceptable-gerbil`, matching the filename-based dispatches in release.yml and reconcile-bridge.yml.
